name: Sofetabart Mipitecan
summary: Sofetabart mipitecan (LY4170156) is Lilly's folate receptor alpha ADC: an Fc-silent anti-FRa antibody carrying exatecan on the PSARlink polysarcosine linker Lilly acquired with Mablink Bioscience (2023). The pivotal trial is FRAmework-01 / GOG-3133 (NCT07213804, 1,630 patients, primary completion 2028-11). Part A randomises 530 platinum-resistant patients 1:1 against investigator's-choice chemotherapy or mirvetuximab, at every level of FRa expression. Parts B and C cover platinum-sensitive disease in combination with bevacizumab. FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation in PROC, and the phase 1 response rate was 50% in 104 patients. Price anchor: Trodelvy's CMS Part B spend of $82,521 per beneficiary (2024). That is the same anchor the book already uses for AZD5335, a rival FRa ADC in the same disease, because Elahere has no CMS row in the book. Uptake anchor: the ramp reuses the book's Enhertu launch fit. Peak penetration is null: Elahere's revenue-implied patient count exceeds the only sourced PROC pool, so it cannot be solved back.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07213804 (FRAmework-01): single-agent ADC dosed every cycle in PROC against chemotherapy or mirvetuximab, which are treated to progression
therapy_mode.note: Oncology treated to progression, so chronic per house convention.

list_price_per_patient.source: python3 /tmp/claude-0/price/lookup.py demand Trodelvy: Part B 2024, $272,318,588 over 3,300 beneficiaries = $82,521 per beneficiary. The same anchor is on the AZD5335 seed (lookup.py seed AZD5335).
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT. The closest marketed comparator is Elahere (mirvetuximab), the Part A comparator arm, but the book has no CMS demand row for it (lookup.py demand %lahere% / %oravtan% return nothing), and no published annual list price was found. Trodelvy is used for two reasons: it is a topo-I ADC in a solid tumour, and it keeps this asset on the same price as AZD5335, the book's other FRa ADC in this disease. Case against: Elahere's launch WAC was $6,220 a vial, about $18,660 to $24,800 per 21-day cycle (Managed Healthcare Executive, https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-of-novel-ovarian-cancer-therapy). Over a real-world median of 8 cycles that is about $174k gross per course, roughly twice this anchor. At this price and gross-to-net, Elahere's $607mm of US 2025 revenue would imply about 14,700 patient-years, which is not plausible. The anchor is therefore probably low for this class.

gross_to_net_pct.source: House convention on a CMS per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py; halving lands at a median 96% of CMS negotiated net prices). The AZD5335 seed carries the same value.
gross_to_net_pct.note: Net is 50% of list. Direction checked: this is the share OFF list. Case against: Part B physician-administered drugs usually carry smaller rebates than Part D drugs.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: MIRASOL (Moore et al., NEJM 2023, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2309169): median PFS with mirvetuximab 5.62 months in FRa-high PROC. Computed as 1 - exp(-12/5.62) = 0.882.
discontinuation_pct.note: Uses the comparator arm's PFS, because sofetabart's phase 1 PFS was not found. The AZD5335 seed uses 0.55, which is unsourced ('a median PFS near a year'); this figure is measured. Case against: a 50% response rate (vs 42% for mirvetuximab in MIRASOL) may mean longer duration on drug. PSOC maintenance-style use in Parts B and C would also run longer.

forecast_start_year.note: Readout in late 2028, then filing in 2029 and a launch in late 2029 or 2030. Breakthrough designation could bring this forward if Part A reads out first. 2030 is the first full year.

exus_multiple.source: ABBV FY2025 10-K (0001551152-26-000008), Elahere net revenues: United States 607, International 83 (from the book's mirvetuximab base_revenue seed). 83/607 = 0.137.
exus_multiple.note: Named comparator: Elahere. Case against: EU approval came only in November 2024 and UK pricing was set in September 2025, so this is an early-launch split. A mature split would probably be higher.

economics_share.source: Mablink Bioscience press release, 2023-10-18: agreement to be acquired by Lilly, bringing the PSARlink platform (https://www.biospace.com/mablink-bioscience-enters-an-agreement-to-be-acquired-by-lilly). The Lilly BTD release (https://investor.lilly.com/news-releases/news-release-details/lillys-sofetabart-mipitecan-receives-us-fdas-breakthrough) describes the asset as Lilly's own.
economics_share.note: No co-development or profit-share partner found. Any milestones or royalties owed to Mablink's former holders are undisclosed and not modelled.

prevalence.note: lookup.py pool 'Ovarian Neoplasms': R-DXD row, SEER 21,010 new US cases in 2026. epidemiology.csv says to use the combined ovary / fallopian tube / peritoneum pool for the fallopian tube and peritoneal tags.

incidence.note: As prevalence: 21,010 a year from SEER.

eligible_pct.source: Value in Health HSD30 / ISPOR 2024 poster 139151, 'Incidence of Platinum-Resistant, Stage III/IV Ovarian Cancer Patients in the US' (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(24)01368-8/fulltext). In 2023, 6,224, 4,329 and 2,901 patients were treated in lines 2, 3 and 4, with 14.7%, 40.5% and 59.1% platinum-resistant. That is 915 + 1,753 + 1,714 = 4,382 PROC patients treated in lines 2 to 4. 4,382 / 21,010 = 0.209.
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the arithmetic. This matches Part A's population: PROC after 3 or fewer prior lines, at all FRa levels, so no FRa cut is applied. It assumes the eventual label is not FRa-restricted. Caveats: the counts are line-treatment events, so one patient can appear in both line 3 and line 4. The ISPOR base is 14,768 stage III/IV cases (IARC), not the book's 21,010. One search summary gave the line-3 count as 2,901, so the second reader should confirm the per-line figures. The pool looks low against Elahere revenue (see penetration). The platinum-sensitive Parts B and C are not modelled.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.note: The incumbent is Elahere, but the book has no CMS beneficiaries row for it and AbbVie discloses no patient count. From revenue: $607mm US (FY2025) divided by about $174k gross per course (WAC $18,660 to $24,800 per cycle times a real-world median of 8 cycles) gives at least 3,490 patient starts a year. That is a lower bound, because net is below WAC. The FRa-high PROC pool on the ISPOR basis is only about 4,382 x 35% = 1,534. The solved share would be above 100%, so the pool and the anchor do not reconcile, and any value here would be a guess. For reference, AZD5335 carries an unsourced 0.30.

ramp_steepness.source: Book's Enhertu launch fit on the AZD5335 seed: CMS Part B beneficiaries of 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105 and 8,410 over 2020 to 2024 give k = 1.08 with a midpoint at 2.2 years (lookup.py demand Enhertu confirms the counts)
ramp_steepness.note: Reused from the closest modelled competitor, AZD5335 (another FRa ADC in PROC). Case against: Enhertu opened a new HER2-low segment, while this asset enters a line where Elahere is already established.
